## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a dynamic geometric structure with deletions, leveraging offline time decomposition and per-node hull maintenance. Requires reasoning about intervals, convex hull construction, and multi-node query aggregation.

## Key Concepts

- Offline dynamic geometry using a segment tree over time
- Per-node 2D convex hulls for max dot product queries
- Handling deletions via time intervals; duplicates via multiplicities

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudocode sketch
class Node { constructor() { this.points = []; this.hull = null; } build() { this.hull = buildHull(this.points); } maxDot(w) { return this.hull ? this.hull.maxDot(w) : -Infinity; } }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle numeric precision in maxDot, especially with near-collinear points?
- How would you adapt to support dynamic updates to W (non-static query vector) efficiently?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests mastery of advanced dynamic trees and path-aggregate maintenance, key for scalable graph analytics in large apps like Discord or Airbnb.

## Key Concepts

- Link-Cut Tree (splay-based)
- Path aggregates: sum and max
- Edge-node representation
- Lazy reversal and access patterns
- Amortized O(log n) operations

## Code Example

```javascript
// Skeleton Link-Cut operations
class Node { constructor(val=0){ this.val=val; this.sum=val; this.max=val; this.left=null; this.right=null; this.parent=null; this.rev=false; } }
function pull(x) { x.sum = x.val + (x.left?.sum ?? 0) + (x.right?.sum ?? 0); x.max = Math.max(x.val, (x.left?.max ?? -Infinity), (x.right?.max ?? -Infinity)); }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle dynamic connectivity with cycles?
- How would you extend to support path min or k-th largest on path?
